author: Walter Scott
title: Ivanhoe; A Romance
edition: Ivanhoe; a Romance, by “the Author of Waverley,” in three volumes, Volume I. Edinburgh: printed for Archibald Constable and Co.; London: Hurst, Robinson, and Co., 1820 (first edition; title page in the scan). Text from the scan-backed, proofread Wikisource transcription of “Ivanhoe (1820 Volume 1).pdf”, chapters I–V. HTML styling, running heads, page-number anchors and footnote reference marks are removed and line-wrap whitespace is reflowed; the edition’s spelling and the transcription’s straight quotation marks are retained. Five transcription errors are corrected to the page scans (printed pp. 39 “severities”, 50 “formed”, 70 “belonged”, 77 “Bois-Guilbert”, 84 “doffed”); the printed misprint “acccomplishment” (p. 63) is retained. Scott’s three “L. T.” footnotes that fall within selections are given as separate paragraphs immediately after the paragraph that cites them. The library text holds the whole three-volume romance (the Dedicatory Epistle and all chapters) with Scott's footnotes; the five corrections apply to the whole work. Blocks 275–416 (Volume I, the chapters printed “CHAPTER VII.” for the second time and “CHAPTER VIII.”, pp. 100–156) were collated on 2026-11-18 against the scan itself (Wikimedia Commons “Ivanhoe (1820 Volume 1).pdf”, its text layer compared word by word and every difference decided on the page image); four readings changed: p. 149 “of his” (transcribed “ofhis”), p. 101 “cup-bearer” (transcribed “cupbearer”; the page breaks it at its hyphen and prints “cup-bearer” twice more), and two marks the transcription supplied that the page does not print, the colon after “country” (p. 109) and the full stop after “pilgrim’s staff” (p. 110); the printed misprint “authoritity” (pp. 100–101) is retained.

rights.basis: First edition published in Edinburgh and London in 1820 (Scott died in 1832); a work published before 1931 is in the US public domain as of 2026. The scan’s title page is dated 1820 and Wikisource marks the transcription PD-old.

acquisition.method: MediaWiki API action=parse (formatversion 2, prop text|revid) for the main page, the Dedicatory Epistle and the 44 chapter subpages in printed order; downloadSha256 hashes the 46 API responses concatenated in that order. From the main page only the title is used (as the level-1 heading IVANHOE; A ROMANCE.); its title-page motto, the publishers' advertisement and the chapter list are left out. From the subpages every transcluded page block is kept, with header templates, licence footer, page-number anchors, zero-width page markers, running heads, the typographic brace in the Epistle's signature the closing printer's imprint, and one stray closing poem tag that the transcription shows as literal text after the first stanza of the Barefooted Friar's song (Volume II, Chapter III; subpage Chapter 17) removed, italic styling dropped and line-wrap whitespace joined (a line break inside a paragraph, as in chapter mottoes, becomes a space). The Dedicatory Epistle and each chapter heading, as printed (the volumes number their chapters afresh, and the 1820 misnumberings such as a second CHAPTER VII. and CHAPTER X. stand), are level-2 headings; the printed end of volume first. and end of volume second. lines stay as paragraphs. Scott's footnotes stay where the transcription places them, at the end of each chapter, in the form [Footnote n: text], with their [n] anchors in the running text. The five declared corrections are applied as exact replacements, each matching once.
